findings.text: Exposes an initializer that prepares an iterator to describe a caller supplied kernel vector list for a given transfer direction and byte budget, marking the iterator kind accordingly and starting at the beginning of the list.

Exposes an initializer that prepares an iterator to describe a caller supplied block vector list for a given transfer direction and byte budget, marking the iterator kind accordingly and starting at the beginning of the list.
Exposes an initializer that prepares an iterator over a folio queue, recording the queue reference, starting slot, intra queue offset and byte budget for the requested direction.
Exposes an initializer that prepares an iterator over paged file content addressed through a tree, recording the tree reference, starting file position and byte budget for the requested direction.
Exposes an initializer that prepares a sink iterator which accepts only read direction and tracks only how many bytes remain to be discarded.

Exposes a query that summarizes address and length alignment of the remaining iterator span, with distinct handling for single buffer, vector like, block, folio queue and tree backed kinds, and a neutral result for other or empty cases.
Exposes a query that summarizes alignment of boundaries between consecutive vector segments within the remaining span, with defined results for single buffer and for misuse.

Exposes a pinning interface that materializes page references for the current iterator position up to caller size and page count bounds, reports the offset inside the first page, and consumes the mapped span from the iterator.
Exposes an allocating variant of the pinning interface that creates its own page pointer storage, releasing it and reporting failure when no bytes can be mapped.
Exposes a page count estimator that bounds how many distinct pages the remaining span touches, honoring a caller supplied maximum and handling all iterator kinds observed.
Exposes a duplication helper that copies iterator state and, for vector like and block kinds, privately duplicates the segment array so the new iterator owns its descriptor storage.

Exposes a helper that obtains a kernel copy of a user supplied vector array, reusing caller provided fast storage when large enough and handling empty lists, excessive counts, allocation failure and compat layout.

Exposes helpers that validate user buffers or vector arrays and establish a ready iterator, using a compact single buffer representation for the one segment case, enforcing accessibility and truncating excessive total length.
Exposes a restore helper that returns an iterator to a previously saved position by reinstating offsets, remaining count and segment accounting for buffer and vector like kinds.

Transfer direction is constrained to read or write for vector initializers, to a single bit for queue and tree initializers, and to read alone for the discard sink; violations are flagged as programming errors.
Plain user vectors and kernel vectors are treated as layout compatible, allowing shared alignment, page counting and duplication logic across both kinds.

Remaining length and intra segment offset together define the unconsumed span; consuming bytes reduces the remainder and advances the offset, while segment pointer and remaining segment count move together to preserve their combined coverage.
User supplied lengths never establish an iterator whose total exceeds a global transfer maximum; overlong totals are truncated and a single overlong buffer length is clamped before iterator creation.
Zero length requests yield neutral results without touching backing storage, including zero alignment, zero page count and zero mapped length.

Traversal of tree backed content for page materialization is performed under read side protection that is acquired before lookup and released after references are taken, with retry handling when entries change under the reader.

Iterator state observed includes a kind tag, a direction marker, a remaining byte count, an intra segment offset, a remaining segment count, and kind specific references to single buffer, vector array, block array, folio queue with slot, or tree with start position, plus a fault control flag.
Saved iterator position observed comprises remaining byte count, intra segment offset and remaining segment count, sufficient to rewind vector like iterators without storing duplicate pointers.

Vector segments are described by base address plus length, block segments by page reference plus page offset plus length, and folio queue entries by owning queue plus slot index plus size, all interpreted relative to the iterator offset.

Vector like and block iterators progress from full span toward exhaustion by shrinking the remainder and sliding within then across segments; reaching the end of a segment resets the intra offset and advances to the next descriptor.

Folio queue iterators progress through slots in order, wrapping to the successor queue when slots are exhausted and resetting the intra queue offset on slot change; an out of range slot at entry moves to the next queue.
Tree backed iterators maintain a logical position as tree start plus accumulated offset; successful page materialization advances that offset and shrinks the remainder by the mapped length.
User facing vector import acts as an entry helper that detects compat mode internally and dispatches to compact or full import paths, returning total imported length or a negative error.

Page pinning helpers act as entry helpers for consumers needing stable page references, accepting caller bounds and returning mapped byte count with first page offset, or zero or negative error when nothing is mappable.

Negative user lengths are rejected as invalid, inaccessible user addresses as fault, allocation failures as out of memory, folio queue offset mismatch as input output error, and non vector use of gap query as warning with saturated result.

Programming misuse triggers diagnostic traps, including invalid direction bits, restore of unsupported kinds, empty vector traversal reaching an impossible state, and missing page storage where required.

Block extraction may return a prefix when later pages carry an interior offset or when a segment ends mid page, requiring the caller to reissue the call for the remainder; folio and tree extraction similarly bound output by available pages.
Distinct kind tags identify kernel vector, block vector, folio queue, tree backed and discard iterators, and govern which associated reference and helper path applies.
Global bounds observed include a maximum segment count for user vectors, a maximum byte count for any single transfer, and page granularity for offsets and page calculations.
